questions.question: A newborn presents with severe hypotonia, poor feeding, and minor dysmorphic features. Methylation analysis reveals loss of maternal expression at chromosome 15q11-q13, confirming Prader-Willi syndrome. Single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) microarray reveals complete maternal isodisomy of chromosome 15. Which of the following meiotic errors, followed by trisomy rescue, is the most likely cause of this genetic finding?
options: Nondisjunction during paternal meiosis I
Nondisjunction during maternal meiosis II
Nondisjunction during maternal meiosis I
Nondisjunction during paternal meiosis II

questions.question: Von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) disease is an autosomal dominant cancer predisposition syndrome. Under normoxic cellular conditions, what is the primary molecular function of the wild-type VHL protein (pVHL)?
options: Phosphorylating retinoblastoma protein (Rb) to maintain cell cycle arrest at the G1/S transition
Binding directly to double-strand DNA breaks to recruit the non-homologous end joining repair machinery
Directing the polyubiquitination and subsequent proteasomal degradation of hypoxia-inducible factor alpha (HIF-α)
Functioning as a transmembrane receptor kinase that sequesters vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF)

questions.question: Williams-Beuren syndrome is a neurodevelopmental disorder caused by a contiguous gene microdeletion on chromosome 7q11.23. Haploinsufficiency of which gene within this deleted region is directly responsible for the cardiovascular abnormalities, specifically supravalvular aortic stenosis, seen in these patients?
options: ELN
LIMK1
GTF2I
CLIP2

questions.question: During X-chromosome inactivation (XCI) in female mammalian embryogenesis, the long non-coding RNA XIST coats the future inactive X chromosome. Which of the following events occurs earliest downstream of XIST RNA coating to establish gene silencing?
options: Hypermethylation of promoter CpG islands across the inactive X chromosome
Incorporation of the atypical histone variant macroH2A into nucleosomes
Complete loss of nuclear matrix attachment regions along the X chromosome
Recruitment of Polycomb repressive complexes (PRC1/PRC2) and insertion of repressive histone marks such as H3K27me3

questions.question: Zellweger syndrome is a severe peroxisome biogenesis disorder caused by pathogenic variants in PEX genes. Which biochemical diagnostic marker in plasma or serum best demonstrates the loss of peroxisomal beta-oxidation function in these patients?
options: Elevated levels of branched-chain amino acids (leucine, isoleucine, and valine)
Elevated levels of succinylacetone and homogentisic acid
Elevated levels of very long-chain fatty acids (VLCFAs) such as hexacosanoic acid (C26:0)
Markedly reduced levels of propionylcarnitine (C3) and methylmalonic acid
